transcript.text: Thank you all for joining me. As you know, we're considering a classroom pilot of an adaptive writing platform for the fall term. The vendor has offered it at no cost, and it can provide individualized writing prompts and feedback to students. Before I approve the proposal, I need your operational findings on several gaps I've identified in the draft. Specifically, we haven't yet specified which grade level will participate, what data settings are appropriate, what teacher support will look like, how we'll handle privacy review, and how we'll orient families. I'd like to go around and hear from each of you on these points. Let's start with our instructional coach -- what are you seeing on the ground in terms of where this platform might fit best, and what teachers would need to make it work?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I should share something important from my coaching notes. I actually observed this platform in two seventh-grade classrooms, and I found that the useful feedback depended on a six-week cycle with one coached teacher-planning session each week. I recorded this in my coaching notes, but they haven't been attached to the draft proposal yet. This directly informs both the grade-level question and the teacher support question.

There are two key requirements: first, student accounts must operate in local-only mode, and identifiable writing data may be retained for exactly 30 days.
